A little note, from me to you

Dear Asmita,

Happy birthday, Fuchhi. I hope today gives you a hundred little reasons to smile — the kind of smile that stays even after the phone screen goes dark.

It's funny how someone can become part of your everyday thoughts even when they live far away. We started with a TikTok conversation, a few messages, and one small exchange of numbers. I didn't know then that those simple moments would become something I would look forward to.

Your quick reactions, your short-tempered moments that soften again, your funny side, and your legendary Kumbhakarna naps have all become little pieces of a story I genuinely enjoy. Please don't ever feel you have to be perfect to be appreciated. You can simply be yourself.

We haven't met face to face yet, and I can't hand you this birthday wish in person. So I made this little corner of the internet carry what I wanted to say: thank you for the conversations, the laughter, and the unexpected happiness in ordinary days.

I hope life is gentle with you. I hope you get the opportunities you quietly wish for, the courage for the difficult days, and people around you who make you feel safe, respected, and valued.

And whenever you look back at this birthday, I hope you remember that someone, from a little distance away, took time to make you smile.

— Someone who is really glad our paths crossed ♡

A few things worth celebrating

Little things that make you, you

You're funny in ways you probably don't even notice.

You can be wonderfully expressive — nobody has to guess when you have an opinion. 😂

You bring your own kind of energy to a conversation, and even from far away, that can brighten an ordinary day.

And beneath all the jokes and Kumbhakarna-level naps, there's a person who deserves to feel valued, respected, and cared for.

Miles apart, still a lovely thought

Until the day we meet…

For now, there are screens between us, messages instead of shared walks, and birthday wishes travelling through the internet.

We haven't met face to face yet, but I hope that one day, if life gives us the chance, we can turn some of these conversations into a real-life memory.

Until then, no pressure and no big promises — just care, respect, good conversations, and reasons to smile.
